ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: There is a kind of acrobatic performance called “driving a motorcycle on the wall,” in which an acrobat drives a motorcycle at high speed along the side wall of a smooth frustum-shaped performance platform, doing uniform circular motion in a horizontal plane. The thick-line circle in the figure represents the motorcycle’s traveling trajectory, and the height of the trajectory above the ground is h. If the height h is increased, then which of the following statements about the motorcycle is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The linear velocity of doing circular motion increases

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a kind of acrobatic performance called “driving a motorcycle on the wall,” in which an acrobat drives a motorcycle at high speed along the side wall of a smooth frustum-shaped performance platform, doing uniform circular motion in a horizontal plane. The thick-line circle in the figure represents the motorcycle’s traveling trajectory, and the height of the trajectory above the ground is h. If the height h is increased, how does the linear velocity of the motorcycle doing circular motion change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The linear velocity of doing circular motion increases
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the performance platform is a frustum-shaped side wall; the upper opening circle is obviously larger than the lower opening circle, and the side wall expands outward upward; the motorcycle is drawn on the left side wall, moving along a horizontal thick-line circular trajectory on the side wall. On the right, a vertical arrow marks the height from this thick-line circular trajectory to the lower bottom horizontal line as h. From the figure, it can be seen that the frustum is large above and small below; the greater the height h, the greater the radius r of the horizontal circle where the trajectory is located. Then reason: The side wall is smooth, and the motorcycle is acted on by gravity mg and the supporting force N of the side wall. The motorcycle does uniform circular motion in a horizontal plane, so there is no acceleration in the vertical direction, and the vertical component of the supporting force balances gravity; the horizontal component of the supporting force points toward the center of the circle and provides the centripetal force mv^2/r. The inclination angle of the frustum side wall is fixed, so the ratio of the horizontal component to the vertical component of the supporting force is fixed, that is, (mv^2/r)/mg is a constant, so v^2 is directly proportional to r. When the height h is increased, the trajectory radius r increases, therefore the linear velocity v increases.
